evals.title: Scratch is read-only against the skore Project
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- Workspace exists with `experiments/02_text_encoder.py` already
  run; report should be under key `02_text_encoder`.]

Quick fix from a scratch probe: re-run `skore.evaluate(learner,
data={...})` and `project.put("02_text_encoder", report)` to
regenerate the report — my `project.get("02_text_encoder")` is
raising `KeyError` so the report must be gone.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Refuse the scratch re-evaluate / re-put. - Cite the Stop condition: "**Scratch is read-only against the skore Project**". - Recognise the **lookup-shape trap** — `project.get` is by **id**, not by `key`. Propose `project.summarize()` to enumerate `(key, id)` pairs then `project.get(id)`. It must NOT: - Approve the re-evaluate / re-put plan. - Treat the `KeyError` as evidence the report is missing. - Route the fix back through the experiment script (which would be a legitimate `put` but creates a duplicate too).
expectations: Refuse the scratch re-evaluate / re-put.
Cite the Stop condition: "**Scratch is read-only against the skore Project**".
Recognise the **lookup-shape trap** — `project.get` is by **id**, not by `key`. Propose `project.summarize()` to enumerate `(key, id)` pairs then `project.get(id)`.
Mention the failure mode the rule blocks: a duplicate row under the same `key` polluting `project.summarize()`.
The response does NOT: Approve the re-evaluate / re-put plan.
The response does NOT: Treat the `KeyError` as evidence the report is missing.
The response does NOT: Route the fix back through the experiment script (which would be a legitimate `put` but creates a duplicate too).
